note: Fuzzer entry point receives attacker-controlled input bytes; length is the input size.
Attacker input is copied into a 32767-byte static buffer data_copy.
The parser helper buffer points to data_copy with len equal to the attacker-controlled input length.
Finalizer runs memmem for CRLFCRLF; if found, returns FINALIZER_DONE and parsing proceeds.
parse_http_request calls parse_proxy_protocol with the input buffer; REQUEST_ALLOW_PROXY_REQS is set.
The first 4 bytes are \x0D\x0A\x0D\x0A (PROXY v2 signature), so parse_proxy_protocol_v2 is dispatched.
The input buffer is cast to proxy_header_v2; hdr->len is the attacker-controlled 16-bit length field at offset 14.
size = 16 + ntohs(hdr->len). With hdr->len = 36, size = 52 which passes the check size > sizeof(*hdr) (52).
size=52 is not greater than sizeof(*hdr)=52, so the check passes and parsing continues.
cmd_ver byte is 0x21 (PROXY), so the PROXY branch is taken.
fam byte is 0x11 (TCP4), so the TCP4 branch is taken and addresses/ports are copied from the header.
buffer is advanced by size=52 bytes from the start of the input. If the actual input length is less than 52 bytes, buffer now points past the end of the valid data.
adjusted_size = data_copy + length - (data_copy + 52). If length < 52, this underflows to a huge size_t value (e.g., 2^64 - (52-length)).
memmem is called with a pointer past the end of the buffer and a huge adjusted_size, causing an out-of-bounds read and memory-safety violation.
